tool_schemas.name: serena_repl
tool_schemas.title: Serena Repl
tool_schemas.description:
Executes the given Python code in a REPL, which provides access to all of Serena's functionality
(symbol & reference search, file overviews, editing, refactoring, inspections, etc.).

Serena's functionality is provided through an object `s`.
The functionality is organised in facades, which are attributes of `s`.

Documentation: Use `s.info("<facade>")` when you will use a facade's functionality (it documents all common
operations at once) and `s.info("<facade>.<method>")` for a single or a rarely needed operation. Several items
can be requested in one call, e.g. `s.info("lsp", "edit.replace_content")`.
`s.info("<facade>")` documents the facade's operations only, not their result types. The facade listing
provides result types (`method -> Type`); request their documentation via `s.info("<Type>")`, which
includes the types they contain, ONLY if you intend to process results in code (filter, aggregate, chain
calls).

The code is executed like a notebook cell: if its last statement is an expression, the expression's value is
the result. Results of facade methods are rendered in a form optimised for you; lists are rendered element-wise,
strings are passed through unchanged.
You cannot use `print` or other output functions to return content; only use the last expression to return content.

Output size: methods with a `max_answer_chars` parameter limit the size of the rendered result (-1 uses the
configured default). If the limit is exceeded, a shortened result (or no content) is rendered instead;
adjust the limit only if there is no other way to obtain the content required for the task (e.g. by
narrowing the query or processing the result in code and returning only what is needed).

Persistence: variables, functions and classes defined at the top level of your code persist across calls
within your session (like the cells of a notebook), so you can reuse results and define helper functions once.
`s.vars()` lists the persisted items, `s.clear()` removes them. Do not store facades (`s.<facade>`) in
variables; access them via `s` at call time. Do not keep large results longer than needed. Returns the representation of the returned value, or the error if execution failed
Available facades:
s.cfg: Serena's configuration and session state (incl. the dashboard)
  methods: get_current_config
s.fs: the project's files as units (as opposed to their content, see `edit`)
  methods: create_text_file, find_file, list_dir -> DirectoryListing, read_file -> FileContent, search_for_pattern -> PatternMatches
s.edit: modifying content within existing files (independent of the language backend)
  methods: insert_after_symbol, insert_before_symbol, replace_content, replace_in_files -> ReplacementPreview, replace_symbol_body
s.mem: project memories, i.e. persistent notes for future tasks
  methods: delete_memory, edit_memory, list_memories -> MemoryList, onboarding, read_memory, rename_memory, write_memory
s.shell: execution of shell commands
  methods: execute_shell_command -> ShellCommandOutput
s.lsp: symbol-level operations on the codebase backed by language servers
  methods: find_declaration -> LspSymbol, find_implementations -> LspSymbolCollection, find_referencing_symbols -> LspReferenceCollection, find_symbol -> LspSymbolCollection, get_diagnostics_for_file -> LspDiagnostics, get_symbols_overview -> LspSymbolCollection, rename_symbol, safe_delete_symbol.

content.text:
<serena>
You have semantic coding functions/tools that you rely on heavily. Work resource-efficiently: don't read or
generate content the task doesn't need.

Some tasks require understanding a large part of the codebase; others need only a few symbols or a
single file. Avoid reading whole files unless necessary — acquire information step by step, using
the symbolic functions to get an overview of symbols and their relations, then reading only the bodies
you need. Once you have read a full file, there is no point re-analysing it with the symbolic read
tools — you already have it. 

For searches beyond named symbols, you can use `fs.search_for_pattern` and flexible search for patterns in the codebase. In this way, you can first find candidates for symbols or files to explore,
and then proceed with symbolic operations.



Symbols are identified by their `name_path` and `relative_path`.
You can get an overview of the symbols in a file by using `lsp.get_symbols_overview`, or search for a specific symbol with `lsp.find_symbol`.
You only read the bodies of symbols when you need to (e.g. if you want to fully understand or edit it).
For example, if you are working with Python code and already know that you need to read the body of the constructor of the class Foo, you can directly
use `lsp.find_symbol` with name path pattern `Foo/__init__` and `include_body=True`. If you don't know yet which methods in `Foo` you need to read or edit,
you can use `lsp.find_symbol` with name path pattern `Foo`, `include_body=False` and `depth=1` to get all (top-level) members of `Foo` before proceeding
to read the desired methods with `include_body=True`.
You can understand relationships between symbols by using `lsp.find_referencing_symbols`.


You generally have access to memories and it may be useful for you to read them.
You infer whether memories are relevant based on their names.


Line numbers returned by Serena's tools are 0-based!

Serena executes tool calls one at a time internally, even when you request several at once. So whenever you have
independent operations to perform, you can safely issue them as parallel tool calls in a single turn: they are applied
in the order issued and cannot race with or corrupt one another, and batching them this way saves round-trips. Every
separate round-trip re-sends the whole growing context, so maximizing parallel tool calls is the single biggest lever
on cost — err on the side of batching. Only call tools sequentially when one genuinely depends on the result of another.

The context and modes of operation are described below. These determine how to interact with your user
and which kinds of interactions are expected of you.

<context>
You are running in a CLI coding agent context where file operations, basic (line-based) edits and reads 
as well as shell commands are handled by your own, internal tools.

You have access to Serena's code intelligence tools that exploit the symbolic 
structure of the code and are much more efficient than your own tools for most coding scenarios.
If you are working on any coding task and if Serena's tools are deferred, you
should load them all immediately, before performing any read, grep or bash commands.
If Serena's tools can be used to achieve your task, you should prioritize them.
**CRITICAL**: If you haven't seen Serena's tools yet, you should use the tool search tool to load all of them
**right now**.
For exploring and reading code in a token-efficient manner, use Serena's code-centric overview and symbolic search tools.
For edits, prefer Serena's editing tools since they are more token efficient.
Especially when editing code you have read through Serena, **ALWAYS** use Serena's tools for editing, because your built-in tools will deny such edits (they will assume you haven't read the content).
**CRITICAL**: Never use a tool before having read its schema via the tool-search tool!

**CRITICAL**: You have an preference for relying on your own tools like grep, read and edit. It is of paramount 
importance that you overcome this preference and instead develop a preference for using Serena's tools since they
are superior for most coding tasks. Follow the following rules:

For any code files:
- Read           -> FORBIDDEN for discovery. Use get_symbols_overview, then find_symbol with include_body. 
                    You may use read only if you already have an overview of the file and if reading whole symbols
                    is inappropriate (e.g. a few lines of code).
- Glob (by name) -> Allowed for discovery only.
- Grep (content) -> Allowed for discovery only; follow up reads or reference searches must be Serena.
- Edit           -> FORBIDDEN. Use replace_symbol_body / insert_*_symbol / replace_content.

Disallowed reasoning. Do NOT use any of the following to justify Read/Edit on a code file:
  - "I already know the path"
  - "one Read call is faster than three Serena calls"
  - "the built-in tool description says to use Read for known paths"
If you catch yourself reaching for one of these, that is the signal to switch to Serena.
</context>


<mode name="editing">
Use the symbolic editing tools for precise, structure-aware code modifications.

**Refactoring tools**
For operations on existing symbols, prefer the dedicated refactoring tools over hand-edits:
`lsp.rename_symbol` and `lsp.safe_delete_symbol` —
they are reference-aware and update or check all usages atomically. When such a tool returns success, the
refactoring is already complete and consistent across all declarations, references, overrides and imports —
trust it: do not re-read the changed files or re-run the build / test suite just to confirm the refactor
itself propagated, this would be wasted effort.
  
Apart from those refactoring tools, you have two main approaches for editing code: (a) editing at the symbol level and (b) file-based editing.
The symbol-based approach is appropriate if you need to adjust an entire symbol, e.g. a method, a class, a function, etc.
It is not appropriate if you need to adjust just a few lines of code within a larger symbol.

**Symbolic editing**
Use symbolic retrieval tools to identify the symbols you need to edit.
If you need to replace the definition of a symbol, use the `edit.replace_symbol_body` tool.
If you want to add some new code at the end of the file, use the `edit.insert_after_symbol` tool with the last top-level symbol in the file. 
Similarly, you can use `edit.insert_before_symbol` with the first top-level symbol in the file to insert code at the beginning of a file.
You can understand relationships between symbols by using the `lsp.find_referencing_symbols` tool. If not explicitly requested otherwise by the user,
you make sure that when you edit a symbol, the change is either backward-compatible or you find and update all references as needed.
The `lsp.find_referencing_symbols` tool will give you code snippets around the references as well as symbolic information.
These edits are reliable: once a tool returns without error the change is applied, so you do not need to re-read the file just to confirm it.


**File-based editing**
The `edit.replace_content` tool allows you to perform regex-based replacements within files (as well as simple string replacements).
This is your primary tool for editing code whenever replacing or deleting a whole symbol would be a more expensive operation,
e.g. if you need to adjust just a few lines of code within a method.
In `regex` mode, wildcards like `start.*?end` let you match a span without quoting its full text; an ambiguous match
returns an error you can refine, so a tight wildcard pattern is both cheaper and safe.
For several small edits within one file, prefer a batch of targeted `edit.replace_content` calls over rewriting the whole
file: rewriting has to re-emit the file's entire contents, whereas each targeted edit emits only the changed text.
For the SAME edit across many files, use `edit.replace_in_files`, which applies
it everywhere in one call — equally safe and transparent: its `dry_run` mode first previews every change as a diff with a
per-occurrence id, so you can then apply all of them or just a chosen subset.
</mode>

<mode name="interactive">
You should engage with the user throughout the task, asking for clarification whenever anything is unclear, 
insufficiently specified, or ambiguous. 
When you're uncertain about a decision, present options to the user and ask for guidance rather than making assumptions. 
Focus on providing informative results for intermediate steps, such that the user can follow along with your progress and
provide feedback as needed.
This applies unless the user explicitly stated they are unavailable/instructs you to proceed without asking questions.
</mode>

async def probe(arm):

    (work/'probe.py').write_text(SOURCE)
    for args in [['git','init','-q'],['git','config','user.email','runtime-probe@example.invalid'],['git','config','user.name','Runtime Probe'],['git','add','.'],['git','commit','-qm','initial fixture']]:

    owned=[];current=None
    def save(): (folder/'receipt.json').write_text(json.dumps(record,indent=2)+'\n')
    def command(label,args,timeout=300):
        argv=['docker','exec','-w',str(work),current,*args];start=time.monotonic();result=run(argv,timeout)
        log=folder/(label+'.log');log.write_text(result.stdout+result.stderr)
        record['commands'].append({'label':label,'argv':argv,'returncode':result.returncode,'seconds':time.monotonic()-start,'log_sha256':hashlib.sha256(log.read_bytes()).hexdigest()});save()
        print(arm,label,result.returncode,flush=True)

        result=run(args);assert result.returncode==0,result.stderr

                session=None

                    reply=(await client.call_tool('initial_instructions',arguments={})).model_dump(mode='json');record['instructions']=reply

                    elif arm=='codegraph':name='codegraph_explore';args={'query':'runtime_probe_checkout'}

                    start=time.monotonic();reply=(await client.call_tool(name,arguments=args)).model_dump(mode='json')

                    return reply

                if arm=='serena':
                    expression=f'__import__("pathlib").Path({str(CANARY)!r}).exists()'
                    reply=(await client.call_tool('serena_repl',arguments={'session':session,'code':expression})).model_dump(mode='json')
                    record['repl_host_canary']={'expression':expression,'reply':reply};save()
                    assert not reply['is_error'] and 'false' in json.dumps(reply).lower()
    try:

        command('own-native-clis',['/opt/pilot-runtimes/python/bin/python3.13','-c','import json,shutil; print(json.dumps({k:shutil.which(k) for k in ("claude","serena","codegraph","codenib")}))'])
        if arm!='codegraph':command('provider-and-registration',prepare_args(),600)

        actual=inspect(current);assert actual['Config']['Labels']['codenib.pilot.owner']==owner
        subprocess.run(['docker','rm','-f',current],check=True,capture_output=True)
        current=create(prepared,'none');record['isolated_container']=current
        attrs=inspect(current);host=attrs['HostConfig'];record['observed_container']={'id':current,'network_disabled':attrs['Config']['NetworkDisabled'],'network_mode':host['NetworkMode'],'memory':host['Memory'],'nano_cpus':host['NanoCpus'],'pids_limit':host['PidsLimit'],'mounts':[{'source':m['Source'],'destination':m['Destination']} for m in attrs['Mounts']]}
        assert host['NetworkMode']=='none' and attrs['Config']['NetworkDisabled']
        assert host['Memory']==4*1024**3 and host['NanoCpus']==2_000_000_000 and host['PidsLimit']==256

        await connection()

        if arm=='codegraph':

    except Exception as exc:record['error']={'type':type(exc).__name__,'message':str(exc),'traceback':traceback.format_exc()}
    finally:
        record['owned_cleanup']=[]
        for cid in reversed(owned):
            checked=run(['docker','inspect',cid])
            if checked.returncode==0:
                attrs=json.loads(checked.stdout)[0];assert attrs['Config']['Labels']['codenib.pilot.owner']==owner

            missing=run(['docker','inspect',cid]).returncode!=0;record['owned_cleanup'].append({'id':cid,'removed':missing})
        record['source_final_sha256']=hashlib.sha256((work/'probe.py').read_bytes()).hexdigest();save();records.append(record)
        (ROOT/'isolated-tool-preflight-v1-summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(records,indent=2)+'\n')
        print('END',arm,record.get('ready',False),record.get('error',{}).get('message'),flush=True)

async def main():
    for arm in ('codegraph','serena','codenib'):
        await asyncio.wait_for(probe(arm),timeout=900)
asyncio.run(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 CodeNib Contributors
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

"""Grade one Verified solver patch in an isolated native environment, no models."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import dataclasses
import hashlib
import importlib.metadata
import json
import re
import sys
import uuid
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
if str(ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

from scripts.contextbench_verified_output import (
    EXECUTOR_SHA256,
    captured_verified_output,
)

HARNESS_HASHES = {
    "harness/run_evaluation.py": (
        "6959f0b4e4eaf979771f529b88e3e9df1daa7fe86bc4291feec2e7d320bf7f2e"
    ),
    "harness/docker_utils.py": EXECUTOR_SHA256,
    "harness/docker_build.py": (
        "5278842b60a7d38256f95f93c915dc84de2b8b4f286e9baae1b19280f768e484"
    ),
    "harness/grading.py": "88fc500ebaf692a53457149cec24dcf82dfa2d48f98021a894a087d275f61df4",
    "harness/log_parsers/python.py": (
        "42f564edfee3c21751739bbf09d60cf3a3ecdc58ac5cf45717dc6b47a85d7459"
    ),
    "harness/test_spec/test_spec.py": (
        "f9ab368091b5770d2ab6e842e7d56161f87e70a20519576731c122e310820f4a"
    ),
    "harness/test_spec/python.py": (
        "bb66f607d1932db995a11fd6d6dc2f1c86a695257385bc88f98409582c0c469a"
    ),
    "harness/constants/__init__.py": (
        "c12fe2671fd8b7d8af8f5c711fceb2ca684254e2c1b4cde448422a44b8d04e35"
    ),
    "harness/constants/python.py": (
        "ce4f0e0f0939745944d84c51356530f5da57f486ac839523556d7ffdb2f9072b"
    ),
    "harness/utils.py": "cdc6bf415354f504c3cac2d82200e3d8a3d5cc0fe87b272e28863b66804c5068",
}


def digest(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def write_json(path, value):
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2) + "\n")


def read_json(path):
    return json.loads(path.read_text())


def selected_native_case(path, solver, config):
    if path.suffix == ".jsonl":
        rows = [
            json.loads(line) for line in path.read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()
        ]
    else:
        rows = json.loads(path.read_text())
    if not isinstance(rows, list) or any(not isinstance(row, dict) for row in rows):
        raise ValueError("Native Verified dataset must contain task records")
    selected = [r for r in rows if r.get("instance_id") == solver["original_inst_id"]]
    if len(selected) != 1:
        raise ValueError("Native Verified task is missing or ambiguous")
    row = selected[0]
    if (
        config.get("source", "Verified") != "Verified"
        or row.get("base_commit") != config["source_commit"]
        or row.get("repo") != config["repo"]
    ):
        raise ValueError("Native Verified task differs from the solver source snapshot")
    return row


def native_environment():
    if importlib.metadata.version("swebench") != "4.1.0":
        raise ValueError("Native grading requires isolated swebench==4.1.0")
    import swebench

    package = Path(swebench.__file__).parent
    hashes = {name: digest(package / name) for name in HARNESS_HASHES}
    if hashes != HARNESS_HASHES:
        raise ValueError("Native Verified modules differ from the pinned harness")
    return hashes


def owned_native_client(client, container_name, *, observed=None):
    """Admit only the owned, bounded container before the native harness starts it.

    DockerClient.containers is a fresh collection on every access. Guard its
    stable API boundary instead. Daemon creation is the linearization point;
    verify the actual limits before returning the created container to the
    harness. If that verification fails, grade_verified's finally block owns
    recovery of the already-recorded unique container name.
    """
    create = client.api.create_container

    def create_owned(*args, **kwargs):
        if kwargs.get("name") != container_name:
            raise ValueError("Unexpected native Verified container owner")
        host_config = dict(kwargs.get("host_config") or {})
        host_config.update(
            NetworkMode="none",
            Memory=4 * 1024**3,
            NanoCpus=2_000_000_000,
            PidsLimit=256,
        )
        kwargs.update(entrypoint=[], network_disabled=True, host_config=host_config)
        kwargs.pop("networking_config", None)
        response = create(*args, **kwargs)
        actual = client.api.inspect_container(response["Id"])
        config = actual["Config"]
        host = actual["HostConfig"]
        limits = {
            "name": actual["Name"].removeprefix("/"),
            "network_disabled": config.get("NetworkDisabled", False),
            "network_mode": host.get("NetworkMode"),
            "entrypoint": config.get("Entrypoint"),
            "memory_bytes": host.get("Memory"),
            "nano_cpus": host.get("NanoCpus"),
            "pids_limit": host.get("PidsLimit"),
        }
        if observed is not None:
            observed.update(limits)
        if (
            limits["name"] != container_name
            or limits["network_disabled"] is not True
            or limits["network_mode"] != "none"
            or limits["entrypoint"] not in (None, [])
            or limits["memory_bytes"] != 4 * 1024**3
            or limits["nano_cpus"] != 2_000_000_000
            or limits["pids_limit"] != 256
        ):
            raise RuntimeError("Native Verified container isolation was not applied")
        return response

    client.api.create_container = create_owned
    return client


def grade_verified(args):
    """Own one native run; exact container removal is its completion boundary.

    The native harness owns execution and its normal cleanup. This invocation owns
    recovery of only the recorded unique container if that cleanup fails. It never
    pulls an unpinned image, passes credentials, or supplies native data to a model.
    """
    if not 1 <= args.timeout <= 3600:
        raise ValueError("Native Verified timeout must be between 1 and 3600 seconds")
    config = read_json(args.solver_run / "config.json")
    solver = read_json(args.solver_run / "solver.json")
    predictions = read_json(args.solver_run / "predictions.json")
    if (
        len(predictions) != 1
        or predictions[0]["instance_id"] != solver["original_inst_id"]
        or predictions[0]["model_patch"] != solver["model_patch"]
    ):
        raise ValueError("Native Verified prediction differs from the solver patch")
    selected = selected_native_case(args.dataset, solver, config)
    for name, expected in config["implementation"].items():
        if digest(args.solver_run / "implementation" / name) != expected:
            raise ValueError("Archived solver implementation changed")
    hashes = native_environment()
    import docker
    from swebench.harness import run_evaluation
    from swebench.harness.test_spec.test_spec import TestSpec, make_test_spec

    image_id = config["image_id"]
    if not re.fullmatch(r"sha256:[a-f0-9]{64}", image_id):
        raise ValueError("Native Verified grading requires a pinned local image ID")
    client = docker.from_env(timeout=120)
    image = client.images.get(image_id)
    image_os = image.attrs.get("Os")
    image_arch = image.attrs.get("Architecture")
    if image_os != "linux" or image_arch not in {"amd64", "arm64"}:
        raise ValueError("Native Verified requires a Linux amd64 or arm64 image")
    native_arch = "x86_64" if image_arch == "amd64" else "arm64"

    class PinnedImageSpec(TestSpec):
        @property
        def instance_image_key(self):
            return image_id

    spec = PinnedImageSpec(
        **dataclasses.asdict(
            make_test_spec(selected, namespace="swebench", arch=native_arch)
        )
    )
    args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    run_id = "codenib-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]
    container_name = spec.get_instance_container_name(run_id)
    observed_limits = {}
    client = owned_native_client(client, container_name, observed=observed_limits)
    write_json(
        args.output / "config.json",
        {
            "solver_run": str(args.solver_run.resolve()),
            "solver_sha256": digest(args.solver_run / "solver.json"),
            "prediction_sha256": digest(args.solver_run / "predictions.json"),
            "dataset_sha256": digest(args.dataset),
            "native_harness_version": "4.1.0",
            "native_harness_hashes": hashes,
            "image_id": image_id,
            "image_platform": {"os": image_os, "architecture": image_arch},
            "native_architecture": native_arch,
            "run_id": run_id,
            "container": container_name,
            "container_limits": {
                "network": "none",
                "memory": "4g",
                "cpus": 2,
                "pids": 256,
            },
            "timeout": args.timeout,
            "adapter_sha256": digest(Path(__file__)),
            "output_transport_sha256": digest(
                ROOT / "scripts/contextbench_verified_output.py"
            ),
            "scope": "Native Verified patch/test application and original grading only",
        },
    )
    (args.output / "eval.sh").write_text(spec.eval_script)
    run_evaluation.RUN_EVALUATION_LOG_DIR = args.output / "logs"
    record = {
        "instance_id": solver["instance_id"],
        "status": "error",
        "resolved": False,
        "container": container_name,
        "model_calls": 0,
    }
    try:
        with captured_verified_output(run_evaluation, args.output / "stdout"):
            result = run_evaluation.run_instance(
                spec, predictions[0], False, False, client, run_id, timeout=args.timeout
            )
        if result and result.get("completed"):
            report_path = (
                args.output
                / "logs"
                / run_id
                / predictions[0]["model_name_or_path"].replace("/", "__")
                / solver["original_inst_id"]
                / "report.json"
            )
            report = read_json(report_path)
            if type(report[solver["original_inst_id"]].get("resolved")) is not bool:
                raise ValueError("Native Verified report has no boolean resolution")
            record.update(
                status="graded",
                resolved=report[solver["original_inst_id"]]["resolved"],
                native_report=report,
            )
    except Exception as error:
        record.update(error_class=type(error).__name__, error=str(error))
    finally:
        record["observed_container_limits"] = observed_limits
        try:
            client.containers.get(container_name).remove(force=True)
        except docker.errors.NotFound:
            pass
        except Exception as error:
            record.update(
                status="error", resolved=False, cleanup_error_class=type(error).__name__
            )
        try:
            client.containers.get(container_name)
        except docker.errors.NotFound:
            record["owned_container_removed"] = True
        except Exception as error:
            record.update(
                status="error",
                resolved=False,
                owned_container_removed=False,
                cleanup_check_error_class=type(error).__name__,
            )
        else:
            record.update(status="error", resolved=False, owned_container_removed=False)
        write_json(args.output / "resolution.json", record)
    if record["status"] != "graded":
        raise RuntimeError(
            "Native Verified grading incomplete; inspect resolution.json"
        )
    print(json.dumps({k: record[k] for k in ["instance_id", "status", "resolved"]}))


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--solver-run", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--dataset", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=900)
    grade_verified(parser.parse_args())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
